# Scalar values and missing values

`RSScalar` is the base for wrappers around length-one R values. The regular
scalar classes hold nonmissing values. Each class declared with
`RSScalarClass()` also has a generated NA subclass and a shared missing
instance at `Class$na`. `RSNull` represents R's `NULL` separately.

## Choose a constructor

Use `Class$new(val)` when the type is known and `val` is nonmissing. A typed
convenience constructor, such as `RSNumber_withValue()`, accepts either a
nonmissing scalar or an NA and returns the matching class. The general
`RSScalar_withValue()` dispatches on the R type, including `NULL`.

```{r}
library(robjc)

direct <- RSNumber$new(3L)
typed <- RSNumber_withValue(3L)
dispatched <- RSScalar_withValue(3L)
stopifnot(direct$isMemberOf(RSNumber))
stopifnot(typed$isMemberOf(RSNumber))
stopifnot(dispatched$isMemberOf(RSNumber))
stopifnot(identical(dispatched$value(), 3L))
```

Regular `Class$new(NA)` is rejected by `RSScalar$initialize()`. When missing
input is possible, use the typed convenience constructor, the general
dispatcher, or `Class$na` directly. The NA companion is shared, so repeated
convenience calls return the same instance.

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(RSNumber_withValue(NA_integer_), RSNumber$na))
stopifnot(identical(RSScalar_withValue(NA_real_), RSNumber$na))
stopifnot(RSNumber$na$isMemberOf(RSNANumber))
```

## `NULL` and typed `NA` differ

`NULL` means there is no R value; `NA` is a missing value of a particular
type. `RSScalar_withValue(NULL)` returns the shared `RSNull$null`, whose
`value()` is `NULL`. A typed NA instead returns the matching `Class$na`.

| R input | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `NULL` | `RSNull$null` |
| `NA` | `RSBoolean$na` |
| `NA_integer_` or `NA_real_` | `RSNumber$na` |
| `NA_character_` | `RSString$na` |
| `NA_complex_` | `RSComplex$na` |
| `factor(NA_character_)` | `RSFactor$na` |
| `as.Date(NA)` | `RSDate$na` |
| `as.POSIXct(NA)` | `RSDateTime$na` |

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(RSScalar_withValue(NULL), RSNull$null))
stopifnot(is.null(RSNull$null$value()))
stopifnot(identical(RSScalar_withValue(NA_character_), RSString$na))
stopifnot(is.na(RSString$na$value()))
```

Each NA companion has one `na_value` chosen when its class is declared. The
wrapper family, rather than every original R storage type, determines the
stored NA: both integer and double missing values use `RSNumber$na`, whose
`value()` is `NA_real_`. The shared NA instance also does not preserve
per-input metadata such as a missing timestamp's time zone. Raw values have
no NA representation and therefore `RSRaw` has no NA companion.

## Date-time values

`RSDateTime` accepts length-one `POSIXct` or `POSIXlt` values and stores a
`POSIXct` value representing the same instant. A specified input time zone is
retained for display. Equality and hashing use the instant, so two time zones
can represent the same scalar value.

```{r}
utc <- RSDateTime_withDateTime(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"))
tokyo <- RSDateTime_withDateTime(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01 21:00:00", tz = "Asia/Tokyo"))
stopifnot(identical(attr(utc$value(), "tzone"), "UTC"))
stopifnot(identical(attr(tokyo$value(), "tzone"), "Asia/Tokyo"))
stopifnot(utc$isEqual(tokyo))
stopifnot(identical(utc$hash(), tokyo$hash()))
```

For declaring a new scalar class and choosing `na_value`, see
`vignette("robjc_class_factories", package = "robjc")`.
